research_scope: Five source-free complete-definition reviews of Noetherian modules, reduced rings, subspace topology and unital ring elements; no corpus/source changes.

amendments.review_rationale: Read the ascending-chain version for all A-submodules of the specified commutative-unital-ring module. Distinguished stabilization from mere existence of maximal elements and recorded index dependence.
amendments.reason: Read entire original formulation and effective references; kept the mathematics of Noetherian characterizations, nilpotence, relative set intersection, and unit identity distinct from defining axioms. No source research.

references.phrase: module M over commutative unital ring A

references.context: Module and order theory: an ascending chain (M_n)_{n≥1} of A-submodules of a fixed A-module M, satisfying M_n⊆M_{n+1} for every n, with equality allowed.
references.reason: Ascending submodule chains are reusable structures; the Noetherian property concerns stabilization of all such chains.

references.disposition: The requirement that every ascending submodule chain stabilizes after a finite index is the defining ascending-chain condition for a Noetherian module, not a separate prerequisite.
This is an equivalent axiom of the Noetherian module meaning and not a dependency on a separate Noetherian module.

amendments.review_rationale: Read the maximal-condition formulation, with quantification over every nonempty collection of A-submodules and maximality under inclusion, not a greatest submodule condition.
amendments.reason: Read entire original formulation and effective references; kept the mathematics of Noetherian characterizations, nilpotence, relative set intersection, and unit identity distinct from defining axioms. No source research.

references.phrase: module M over commutative unital ring A

references.disposition: The nonempty quantifier scopes the collection over which the maximal-condition axiom is asserted; it does not introduce a separately defined kind of module.

references.context: Order theory: a maximal element N of a nonempty partially ordered family F of submodules ordered by inclusion, meaning no member of F strictly contains N; unlike a greatest element, N need not contain all members of F.
references.reason: Maximal elements in partially ordered collections are independently reusable; the assertion that every nonempty family has one is the defining Noetherian condition.

references.disposition: The chosen member need not contain all other members of the collection; finite generation is not inserted as a separate axiom.

amendments.review_rationale: Read reduced associative ring through nonexistence of nonzero nilpotent elements, quantified over positive exponents and all elements.
amendments.reason: Read entire original formulation and effective references; kept the mathematics of Noetherian characterizations, nilpotence, relative set intersection, and unit identity distinct from defining axioms. No source research.

references.context: Algebra: element r of an associative ring R (identity not required) is nilpotent if r^n=0 for some positive integer n. Do not restrict to commutative rings without justification.
references.reason: Nilpotent elements are a reusable notion distinct from reduced rings and nilpotent ideals.

references.disposition: The assertion that zero is the only nilpotent ring element is exactly the defining reducedness condition; the nilpotent-element prerequisite is classified separately.
Reduced rings may contain nonzero zero divisors; lack of nilpotents is weaker than domain condition.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed general subspace topology from intersections of ambient open sets with arbitrary subset, including empty subset and the resulting induced topological space.
amendments.reason: Read entire original formulation and effective references; kept the mathematics of Noetherian characterizations, nilpotence, relative set intersection, and unit identity distinct from defining axioms. No source research.

references.context: Set theory: binary intersection A∩U={x:x∈A and x∈U} of two subsets of a common ambient set X, applied here to arbitrary A⊆X and open U∈τ.
references.reason: Set intersection is a reusable set operation; the induced topology is generated by all such relative intersections.

references.disposition: The family τ_A={A∩U:U∈τ} is the topology being defined on A, not an independently assumed topology or a recursive self-link.
General topological-space convention admits an empty subspace and does not impose a nonempty hypothesis.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed unit of associative unital ring as element possessing a two-sided multiplicative inverse, distinguishing an invertible element from the ring's identity element.
amendments.reason: Read entire original formulation and effective references; kept the mathematics of Noetherian characterizations, nilpotence, relative set intersection, and unit identity distinct from defining axioms. No source research.

references.context: Ring theory: specified two-sided multiplicative identity 1_R in an associative ring R, satisfying 1_Rr=r1_R=r for all r∈R, with no commutativity requirement.
references.reason: The existence and identity of ring unity is a reusable property; the indexed associative-ring base allows rings without one.

references.disposition: The equations uv=vu=1_R for some v∈R are the defining two-sided invertibility criterion of the unit u, not a prerequisite assertion that u is already a unit.

references.phrase: a unit need not equal unity
references.disposition: The identity element is itself a unit but most units in a ring need not be the identity.
